about: A verse whose draft the rules of meanings.py cannot bring to the style sheet: the whole meaning (as it is published), with its reason.

8.26.text: May Indra have the three worlds, and the gods receive the oblations. If you wish to live, go to Pātāla.
8.26.why: the draft shared ten or more words with Pargiter (1904); reworded, the sense kept exactly (style.md §1)

5.120.text: “Whoever defeats me in battle, whoever takes away my pride, whoever is equal to me in strength in the world, he will be my husband.”
5.120.why: the draft shared ten or more words with Pargiter (1904); reworded, the sense kept exactly (style.md §1)

9.41.text: Some asuras perished, some fled the great battle, and the rest Kālī, Śivadūtī and the lion, king of beasts, devoured.

11.3.text: O Devī, who take away the suffering of those who come to you for refuge, be gracious! Be gracious, Mother of all the world! Be gracious, Mistress of the universe, and protect the universe! You, O Devī, rule over all that moves and is still.
11.3.why: the draft shared ten or more words with Pargiter (1904); reworded, the sense kept exactly (style.md §1)

11.34.text: O Devī, be gracious; protect us always from fear of enemies, just as you have done now, at once, by slaying the asuras. Quickly put an end to the sins of every world and to the great calamities born of the ripening of evil portents.
11.34.why: the draft shared ten or more words with Pargiter (1904); reworded, the sense kept exactly (style.md §1)

3.7.text: With his keen-edged sword he struck the lion on the head and, very swift, struck the Devī too on her left arm.

3.25.text: He too, of great might, in his anger trampled the surface of the earth with his hooves, flung high mountains with his two horns and bellowed.

5.129.text: So go, and respectfully report to the lord of the asuras everything I have told you; and let him do what is fitting.

3.40.text: Having spoken thus, she sprang up and mounted that great asura; pressing his neck down with her foot, she struck him with her trident.
